title: 认识更多人，而不是死磕一个：两个人合不合得来，见面之前预测不出来
englishTitle: Getting to know more people rather than fixating on just one: You can’t predict compatibility before meeting someone
originalText:
### 1. 认识更多人，而不是死磕一个：两个人合不合得来，见面之前预测不出来
<!-- 成本标签: 钱=0 时间=中 毅力=些 收益=中 口径=时间 -->
- 成本：不花钱。时间花在多认识几个人上，别反复琢磨同一个人。难在忍住不死磕。
- 说人话：两场闪电约会研究让人在见面前填了 100 多项择偶问卷。问卷只能算出谁普遍容易喜欢别人、谁普遍受欢迎，算不出这两个人之间来不来电。合不合得来只有见了面才知道。所以多认识几个人，比押在一个人身上划算。
- 收益：两场闪电约会研究里，参与者见面前先填了 100 多项与择偶有关的自陈量表（自己给自己打分的问卷）。研究者用随机森林模型（一种找规律的算法）来算。能算出「一个人整体上有多容易喜欢别人」，这些问卷能说明其中 4%–18% 的方差，方差就是人与人之间的差别，问卷只能说明其中一小部分。也能算出「一个人整体上有多受欢迎」，能说明 7%–27%。但「这两个具体的人之间来不来电」算不出来，会前的特质和偏好怎么组合都算不出来。同一批研究者更早还做过一项闪电约会实验。参与者会前自己报了理想型偏好，比如看重外貌还是看重经济前景。这个偏好预测不了他们在现场对具体某个人的兴趣
- 证据等级：A
- 来源：Joel S, Eastwick PW, Finkel EJ (2017). Is romantic desire predictable? Machine learning applied to initial romantic attraction. Psychological Science, 28(10), 1478-1489. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797617714580>；Eastwick PW, Finkel EJ (2008). Sex differences in mate preferences revisited: do people know what they initially desire in a romantic partner? Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 94(2), 245-264. <https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.94.2.245>
- 备注：两项研究只说明「见面之前算不出来」，没说「怎么努力都没用」。合不合得来只能见了面才知道，所以把时间花在多认识几个人上，每个都真正见一面，比全押在一个人身上划算。研究对象都是欧美大学生。中国的婚恋环境不一样，套到自己身上要打折

### 1. Getting to know more people rather than fixating on just one: You can’t predict compatibility before meeting someone
<!-- Cost Tag: Money=0 Time=Med Willpower=Some Benefit=Med Metric=Time -->

- Cost: No cost at all. Spend time getting to know several people instead of obsessing over just one. The hard part is resisting the urge to fixate on a single person.
- In plain terms: Two speed-dating studies asked participants to fill out over 100 questionnaires about their preferences in a partner before any meetings took place. These questionnaires could only reveal how likely someone is to like others in general, and how popular they tend to be — they couldn’t predict whether two specific people would hit it off. Compatibility can only be determined by meeting in person. Therefore, it’s far more worthwhile to get to know multiple people than to bet everything on just one.
- Benefit: In both speed-dating studies, participants completed more than 100 self-report questionnaires related to partner preferences prior to meeting potential matches. Researchers then applied a random forest model — an algorithm designed to detect patterns — to analyze the data. This model could predict “how likely an individual is to like others overall,” with the questionnaires accounting for 4%–18% of the variance in such tendencies; this represents only a small fraction of the total differences between individuals. It could also predict “how popular an individual tends to be,” explaining 7%–27% of variance. However, it completely failed to predict whether two specific individuals would be compatible; no combination of pre-meeting traits or preferences could be used to forecast their mutual attraction. Earlier, the same research team conducted another speed-dating experiment where participants reported their own ideal preferences — whether they valued physical appearance or financial prospects more. Even this information couldn’t predict how interested they’d be in a particular person during the actual date.
- Evidence grade: A
- Sources:Joel S, Eastwick PW, Finkel EJ (2017). Is romantic desire predictable? Machine learning applied to initial romantic attraction. Psychological Science, 28(10), 1478-1489. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797617714580>; Eastwick PW, Finkel EJ (2008). Sex differences in mate preferences revisited: do people know what they initially desire in a romantic partner? Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 94(2), 245-264. <https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.94.2.245>
- Notes: Both studies clearly state that compatibility cannot be predicted before meeting someone — they do not claim that all efforts to predict it are futile. Since true compatibility can only be determined by face-to-face interaction, it makes far more sense to invest time in meeting multiple people individually rather than placing all hopes on just one. Keep in mind that all study participants were university students from Western countries; China’s dating environment differs significantly, so these findings should be applied with some caution.

title: 对方明确拒绝之后就停下，继续纠缠是治安违法，不是「诚意」
englishTitle: Stop after a clear refusal — continued pursuit is a public order violation, not “sincerity”
originalText:
### 2. 对方明确拒绝之后就停下，继续纠缠是治安违法，不是「诚意」
<!-- 成本标签: 钱=0 时间=少 毅力=是 收益=中 口径=自由 -->
- 成本：不花钱，也不花时间。难在忍住：不再发消息，不再去等人。
- 说人话：对方明确说了拒绝，你还发消息、还去等人，2026 年 1 月起就是治安违法。可以拘留 5 日以下，或者罚 1000 元以下。情节较重的拘留 5 到 10 日。公安还可以下令禁止你接触对方，违反了再拘留 5 到 10 日。
- 收益：2026 年 1 月 1 日起施行的治安管理处罚法，把纠缠、跟踪单列成一项。条文写的是「多次发送淫秽、侮辱、恐吓等信息或者采取滋扰、纠缠、跟踪等方法，干扰他人正常生活的」。这种行为处五日以下拘留，或者一千元以下罚款。情节较重的，处五日以上十日以下拘留，可以并处一千元以下罚款。这一项还多一层：经公安机关负责人批准，可以责令行为人在一定期限内禁止接触被侵害人。违反禁止接触规定的，再处五日以上十日以下拘留
- 证据等级：A
- 来源：全国人大常委会 (2025 修订). 治安管理处罚法（第五十条第一款第五项、第二款）. <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699863.shtml>（最高人民检察院转载）
- 备注：「死追到底会感动对方」没有任何研究支持，但拘留和禁止接触令是白纸黑字的。留下的记录还会影响考公、考编、政审，还有一部分职业的从业资格。追一个人和骚扰一个人的界线，不看你怎么想，看对方有没有明确说过拒绝
englishText:
### 2. Stop after a clear refusal — continued pursuit is a public order violation, not “sincerity”
<!-- Cost Tag: Money=0 Time=Low Willpower=Yes Benefit=Med Metric=Freedom -->
- Cost: No cost at all, neither financial nor time-related. The hard part is self-restraint: refraining from sending further messages or waiting around for the other person.
- In plain terms: If someone has clearly refused you, and you still send messages or wait for them, as of January 2026 this constitutes a violation of public order laws. Offenders may be detained for up to 5 days or fined up to 1000 yuan. For more serious cases, detention ranges from 5 to 10 days. Police can also issue orders barring the offender from contacting the other person; any violation of such orders results in an additional 5–10 days of detention.
- Benefit: The Public Security Administration Punishment Law, effective 1 January 2026, explicitly lists persistent pursuit and stalking as separate violations. The relevant clause states that “repeatedly sending obscene, insulting, threatening or similar messages, or using harassment, stalking and other methods to interfere with another person’s normal life” is punishable by up to 5 days of detention or a fine of up to 1000 yuan. For more serious cases, the penalty is 5–10 days of detention, with a possible fine up to 1000 yuan. This law also adds an extra provision: with approval from a senior police official, offenders can be ordered to refrain from contacting the victim for a set period; any violation of this order incurs an additional 5–10 days of detention.
- Evidence grade: A
- Sources: Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (revised in 2025). Public Security Administration Punishment Law (Article 50, Paragraph 1, Item 5, Paragraph 2). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699863.shtml> (Reprinted by Supreme People's Procuratorate of China)
- Notes: There is no research evidence supporting the claim that “persistent pursuit can win over the other person”; however, detention and contact bans are explicitly stipulated by law. These records also affect eligibility for civil service exams, background checks, and certain professional licenses. The line between pursuing someone and harassing them is not defined by the perpetrator’s intentions, but by whether the other person has clearly expressed refusal.

title: 判断对方有没有兴趣，看行为不看「信号」：谁主动、谁安排、谁跟进
englishTitle: Judging whether someone is interested: focus on actions, not “signals” — who initiates, plans, and follows up
originalText:
### 3. 判断对方有没有兴趣，看行为不看「信号」：谁主动、谁安排、谁跟进
<!-- 成本标签: 钱=0 时间=少 毅力=些 收益=中 口径=时间 -->
- 成本：不花钱，也不花多少时间。难在改习惯：别再琢磨对方的表情和语气，改成记录事实。
- 说人话：让 52 对陌生男女聊十来分钟，再互相判断对方有没有在调情。结果是「对方没在调情」判得比较准，「对方在调情」反而看不出来。换成 261 个人看视频判断，结论一样。所以别猜表情和语气，看行为：谁主动发起，谁安排下一次，你不推进时对方跟不跟进。
- 收益：两项研究测了人识别调情的准确率。第一项让 52 对互不相识的异性两两交谈 10 到 12 分钟。谈完各自报告自己有没有在调情，也报告觉得对方有没有在调情。结果是「没有发生调情的互动被判断得更准，发生了调情的互动反而判断得更差」。第二项用 26 段一分钟的视频，给 261 名旁观者判断，结论一致。人能比较可靠地看出「对方没在调情」，却很难看出「对方在调情」
- 证据等级：B
- 来源：Hall JA, Xing C, Brooks S (2015). Accurately detecting flirting: error management theory, the traditional sexual script, and flirting base rate. Communication Research, 42(7), 939-958. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0093650214534972>；Perilloux C, Kurzban R (2015). Do men overperceive women's sexual interest? Psychological Science, 26(1), 70-77. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797614555727>（争议方）
- 备注：争议。另有研究认为，不是男性高估了女性的性意图，而是女性填问卷时把自己的意图报低了。到底谁判断得更准，仍无定论。但两派都同意一件事：从表情、语气这类细微线索反推对方心思，准确率很低。看得见的行为要可靠得多：对方是否主动发起，是否安排下一次，是否在你不推进时也跟进
englishText:
### 3. Judging whether someone is interested: focus on actions, not “signals” — who initiates, plans, and follows up
<!-- Cost Tag: Money=0 Time=Low Willpower=Some Benefit=Med Metric=Time -->
- Cost: This requires no money or much time. The real challenge is breaking old habits: stop trying to interpret facial expressions and tone, and instead record observable behaviors.
- In plain terms: In one study, 52 pairs of strangers of opposite genders chatted for about 10 minutes, then tried to determine whether each other was flirting. The results showed they were fairly accurate at spotting when no flirting was occurring, but struggled to identify actual flirting. A second experiment using video evaluations reached the same conclusion. Therefore, rather than guessing based on expressions or tone, pay attention to actions: who initiates contact, who schedules future meetings, and whether they follow up when you don’t make the first move.
- Benefit: Two studies examined how accurately people can recognize flirting. The first involved 52 unrelated male-female pairs conversing for 10–12 minutes; afterward, each participant reported whether they themselves were flirting and whether they believed their partner was. The results indicated that interactions without any flirting were identified more reliably, while those involving actual flirting were harder to detect. The second study used 26 one-minute video clips and 261 observers, yielding similar findings. In short, people can fairly reliably tell when someone is not flirting, but they struggle to detect when flirting is happening.
- Evidence grade: B
- Sources:Hall JA, Xing C, Brooks S (2015). Accurately detecting flirting: error management theory, the traditional sexual script, and flirting base rate. Communication Research, 42(7), 939-958. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0093650214534972>; Perilloux C, Kurzban R (2015). Do men overperceive women's sexual interest? Psychological Science, 26(1), 70-77. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797614555727> (Disputing Party)
- Notes: This topic remains debated. Some research suggests the issue isn’t that men overestimate women’s sexual intentions, but that women tend to underreport their own intentions on surveys. There is still no consensus on which group judges more accurately. Nevertheless, both viewpoints agree on one point: relying on subtle cues such as facial expressions or tone to infer someone’s thoughts yields poor results. Observable behaviors — such as who initiates contact, plans future meetings, and follows up without prompting — are far more reliable indicators.

title: 关系好不好，主要看你自己在这段关系里的感受，不是看对方条件
englishTitle: Whether a relationship is good or not depends mainly on how you feel within it, not on your partner’s attributes.
originalText:
### 4. 关系好不好，主要看你自己在这段关系里的感受，不是看对方条件
<!-- 成本标签: 钱=0 时间=少 毅力=些 收益=中 口径=时间 -->
- 成本：不花钱，也不花多少时间。难在改视角：把择偶清单收起来，改成看相处过程。
- 说人话：最能说明关系好不好的，是你自己的感受，不是对方的条件。比如你觉得对方认不认真、欣不欣赏你，你们吵得多不多。你自己的感受比伴侣的说法管用二到四倍。但这段关系往后变好还是变坏，任何问卷都基本算不出来。
- 收益：29 个实验室、43 份纵向配对数据的机器学习分析，纵向就是跟着同一批伴侣一路记录。最能预测关系质量的几项，全部来自当事人对这段关系的感受：感觉到对方的承诺、欣赏、性满意度、感觉到对方满意、冲突。跟个人有关的几项里最强的是生活满意度、负面情绪、抑郁、回避型依恋、焦虑型依恋。关于关系的这些项，在刚开始调查时最多能解释 45% 的方差。方差指伴侣与伴侣之间关系质量的差别，45% 是其中能用这些项说清的部分。到研究结束时最多解释 18%。而且「自己报告的那些项」的预测力，是「伴侣报告的那些项」的二到四倍。在自己报告的关系感受之外，再把个体差异和伴侣的报告加进来，没有多出任何预测力
- 证据等级：A
- 来源：Joel S, Eastwick PW, Allison CJ, et al. (2020). Machine learning uncovers the most robust self-report predictors of relationship quality across 43 longitudinal couples studies. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 117(32), 19061-19071. <https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1917036117>
- 备注：同一项研究还发现，这段关系在研究期间是变好还是变坏，用问卷里任何一组自评指标都基本算不出来。所以判断眼下这段关系好不好，问自己的感受比核对对方的条件清单准，但别指望能预测它以后会怎样。关系好坏和身体好坏连在一起的那笔账，见本节第 17 条（把关系好坏当成一笔健康账）。
englishText:
### 4. Whether a relationship is good or not depends mainly on how you feel within it, not on your partner’s attributes.
<!-- Cost Tag: Money=0 Time=Low Willpower=Some Benefit=Med Metric=Time -->
- Cost: There is no monetary cost, nor does it require much time. The real challenge lies in shifting your perspective: put aside your checklist of ideal partner traits and instead focus on how you interact with each other.
- In plain terms: The best indicator of a healthy relationship is your own feelings toward it, not your partner’s qualifications. For instance, whether you perceive your partner as attentive and appreciative of you, or how often you argue. Your personal feelings carry two to four times more weight than what your partner says about the relationship. However, no questionnaire can reliably predict whether the relationship will improve or deteriorate over time.

### 5. To build closeness, have two people take turns answering a series of progressively deeper questions — no script needed
<!-- Cost Tag: Money=0 Time=Low Willpower=No Benefit=Low Metric=Time -->
- Cost: No cost involved. It takes 45 minutes to complete.
- In plain terms: Pair two strangers up and have them take turns answering 36 questions grouped into three levels of depth. After 45 minutes, their sense of closeness is noticeably higher than in a control group that simply chatted for the same amount of time. What drives this effect is the act of taking turns to share honest thoughts at increasing levels of depth, not any pre-planned conversational script. Keep in mind this measure only captures short-term closeness, and does not guarantee the development of a long-term relationship.
- Benefit: This method pairs two unfamiliar people to answer 36 questions in total, arranged in three tiers of increasing depth. The questions range from “Who is the person you’d most like to invite for dinner?” to “When was the last time you cried in front of someone?” After 45 minutes, the participants report a higher sense of closeness compared to those who only chatted for the same duration. Their reported closeness also exceeds the average rating college students give to their closest real-life relationships.
- Evidence grade: B
- Sources:Aron A, Melinat E, Aron EN, Vallone RD, Bator RJ (1997). The experimental generation of interpersonal closeness: a procedure and some preliminary findings. Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin, 23(4), 363-377. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0146167297234003>
- Notes: Only one experiment has been conducted so far, with college students as participants. It measures short-term closeness only, not whether a lasting relationship can form. The core mechanism at work here is that closeness grows when two people take turns sharing genuine personal details at progressively deeper levels — rather than relying on scripts, tricks or one-sided efforts. The key takeaway for practical use is to “share something honest about yourself, then ask a similarly personal question back”, and make sure both parties get a turn to do so.

title: 异地不比同城差，真正的坎是搬到一起之后的头三个月
englishTitle: Long-distance relationships aren’t worse than local ones — the real challenge comes in the first three months after moving in together
originalText:
### 6. 异地不比同城差，真正的坎是搬到一起之后的头三个月
<!-- 成本标签: 钱=多 时间=多 毅力=是 收益=中 口径=时间 -->
- 成本：要花路费，还要花来回路上的时间。见面次数比同城少。难在长期扛住见不着面。
- 说人话：异地在分开期间反而更稳，因为见得少，容易把对方想得比实际好。真正的坎在搬到一起之后。追踪数据里约一半异地伴侣走到了同城这一步，另一半在分开期间就结束了。重聚的这一半里，三分之一在 3 个月内分手。
- 收益：两项研究的结论一致。异地恋在分开期间反而比同城恋更稳定。原因是异地关系里把对方想得比实际更好的程度明显更高，研究测的是理想化失真、浪漫爱、关系回忆、感知到的一致这几项。而且见面越少，想得越美。但这种稳定只在双方仍然分开时成立，一旦变成同城，异地伴侣更容易分手。追踪异地转同城的那项研究给出的比例是：约一半异地伴侣走到了搬到一起这一步，另一半在分开期间就结束了。在重聚的这一半里，三分之一在重聚后 3 个月内分手。分开期间见面间隔越长、理想化越强，重聚后越不稳
- 证据等级：B
- 来源：Stafford L, Merolla AJ, Castle JD (2006). When long-distance dating partners become geographically close. Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, 23(6), 901-919. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0265407506070472>；Stafford L, Merolla AJ (2007). Idealization, reunions, and stability in long-distance dating relationships. Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, 24(1), 37-54. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0265407507072578>；Dargie E 等 (2015). Journal of Sex & Marital Therapy, 41(2), 181-202. <https://doi.org/10.1080/0092623X.2013.864367>（备注里那项异地研究）
- 备注：对象是美国大学生的恋爱关系，不含婚姻，年代也较早，绝对比例别直接套。另一项研究调查了 717 人异地、425 人同城。两类关系的质量差别很小，关系好不好主要看两个人各自的情况和这段关系本身。所以决定要不要异地时，别拿「异地一定散」当理由。要提前准备的是重聚后那几个月，那时自主空间变少，彼此了解变多，冲突和吃醋也变多

### 6. Long-distance relationships aren’t worse than local ones — the real challenge comes in the first three months after moving in together
<!-- Cost Tag: Money=High Time=High Willpower=Yes Benefit=Med Metric=Time -->
- Cost: There are travel expenses to consider, plus the time spent traveling back and forth. Couples see each other far less often than those living in the same city, making it difficult to maintain the relationship over the long term without regular contact.
- In plain terms: Long-distance relationships actually tend to be more stable while the couple remains apart, since seeing each other infrequently allows each person to idealize the other. The real difficulty emerges only after they move in together. Data shows that roughly half of long-distance couples eventually transition to living locally, while the other half end their relationship while still apart. Among those who reunite, one-third break up within three months of moving together.
- Benefit: Two separate studies reach the same conclusion: long-distance relationships are generally more stable than local ones while the couple remains separated. This stability stems from a significantly higher degree of idealization — meaning each partner tends to view the other more favorably than reality warrants. The studies measured factors such as idealized distortion, romantic love, relationship memories, and perceived similarity. Moreover, the less frequently couples meet, the more positively they tend to view each other. However, this stability holds only while they remain apart; once they live in the same city, long-distance couples are far more likely to split up. One longitudinal study found that about half of long-distance couples eventually moved in together, while the other half ended their relationship while still apart. Of those who reunited, one-third broke up within three months of living together. The longer the intervals between visits while apart, and the greater the degree of idealization, the less stable the relationship tends to be after reuniting.
- Evidence grade: B
- Sources: Stafford L, Merolla AJ, Castle JD (2006). When long-distance dating partners become geographically close. Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, 23(6), 901-919. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0265407506070472>; Stafford L, Merolla AJ (2007). Idealization, reunions, and stability in long-distance dating relationships. Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, 24(1), 37-54. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0265407507072578>; Dargie E et al. (2015). Journal of Sex & Marital Therapy, 41(2), 181-202. <https://doi.org/10.1080/0092623X.2013.864367> (Remarks on the off-site study)
- Notes: These findings are based on romantic relationships among American university students, excluding married couples, and date back to an earlier era; thus, absolute percentages should not be applied directly to current populations. Another study surveyed 717 long-distance couples and 425 local couples, finding only minimal differences in overall relationship quality between the two groups. Ultimately, relationship success depends on the individuals involved and the nature of their bond itself, rather than physical distance. The key takeaway is this: do not assume that long-distance relationships are destined to fail. Instead, couples should prepare for the initial months after reuniting, when personal independence diminishes, mutual understanding increases, and conflicts or jealousy are more likely to arise.

title: 先看登记数据再听长辈：结婚率、离婚率各是什么口径
englishTitle: Check registration statistics before listening to elders: what do “marriage rate” and “divorce rate” actually mean?
originalText:
### 7. 先看登记数据再听长辈：结婚率、离婚率各是什么口径
<!-- 成本标签: 钱=0 时间=少 毅力=否 收益=小 口径=时间 -->
- 成本：不花钱。读一遍民政部年度公报里的婚姻登记那一段，几分钟。
- 说人话：2024 年全国结婚登记 610.6 万对，比上一年少了两成，离婚 351.3 万对。网上说离婚率过半，是拿这两个数一除，约 57.5%。可离婚的和结婚的不是同一批人，不能读成一半婚姻会离。公报里的结婚率 4.3‰、离婚率 2.5‰，是除以全国人口算的。
- 收益：2024 年全国依法办理结婚登记 610.6 万对，比上年下降 20.5%，结婚率 4.3‰。同年依法办理离婚手续 351.3 万对，其中民政部门登记离婚 262.2 万对，法院判决和调解离婚 89.1 万对，离婚率 2.5‰。公报注明，结（离）婚率 = 当年结（离）婚对数 / 当年平均总人口数 × 1000‰。这是「粗率」，分母是全体人口，不是已婚人口
- 证据等级：A
- 来源：民政部 (2025). 2024 年民政事业发展统计公报（五（二）1 婚姻登记服务、注释 5），网页版与 PDF 版. <https://www.mca.gov.cn/n1288/n1294/n1554/c1662004999980006190/content.html>、<https://www.mca.gov.cn/gdnps/n2445/n2451/n2458/n2681/c1662004999980006189/attr/400985.pdf>
- 备注：网上常见的「离婚率 50% 以上」，是拿当年离婚的对数除以当年结婚的对数，351.3 / 610.6 ≈ 57.5%。这叫「离结比」。相除的两个数不是同一批人，公报里也没有这个指标，所以不能读成「一半婚姻会离」。要算「一段婚姻最后离掉的概率」，得盯住同一批结婚的人一路统计下去，这种官方数据本节没找到
englishText:
### 7. Check registration statistics before listening to elders: what do “marriage rate” and “divorce rate” actually mean?
<!-- Cost Tag: Money=0 Time=Low Willpower=No Benefit=Low Metric=Time -->
- Cost: None. It takes just a few minutes to read the section on marriage registration in the annual report from the Civil Affairs Bureau.
- In plain terms: In 2024, 6.106 million couples got married nationwide, a 20.5% drop from the previous year. Meanwhile, 3.513 million divorces were finalized. The oft‑quoted claim that “more than half of marriages end in divorce” comes from dividing these two numbers, yielding roughly 57.5%. The exact figures are 351.3 divorces and 610.6 marriages for that year. However, the two groups of people are not the same, so this figure cannot be interpreted as “half of all marriages end in divorce.” The report also lists a marriage rate of 4.3‰ and a divorce rate of 2.5‰; both use the total population as the denominator, not just married individuals.
- Benefit: In 2024, 6.106 million marriages were legally registered, representing a 20.5% decrease from 2023; the corresponding marriage rate was 4.3‰. That same year, 3.513 million divorces were processed: 2.622 million through civil registration and 0.891 million via court rulings or mediation, giving a divorce rate of 2.5‰. The report defines the marriage (or divorce) rate as the number of marriages (or divorces) in a given year divided by the average annual population, multiplied by 1000‰. This is a “crude rate” that uses the whole population as its base.
- Evidence grade: A
- Sources:Ministry of Civil Affairs of China (2025). 2024 Statistical Bulletin on the Development of Civil Affairs (V (II) 1 Marriage Registration Service, Note 5), web version and PDF version. <https://www.mca.gov.cn/n1288/n1294/n1554/c1662004999980006190/content.html>, <https://www.mca.gov.cn/gdnps/n2445/n2451/n2458/n2681/c1662004999980006189/attr/400985.pdf>
- Notes: The common online figure of “over 50% divorce rate” is obtained by dividing the number of divorces by the number of marriages for the same year (351.3 ÷ 610.6 ≈ 57.5%). This ratio is known as the “divorce‑to‑marriage ratio.” Because the two sets of individuals are not identical and the report does not list such a metric, it cannot be taken as “half of all marriages end in divorce.” To calculate the actual probability that a given marriage eventually ends in divorce, one would need longitudinal data tracking the same cohort of newlyweds — data not available in this report.

originalText:
### 8. 把健康收益算进去，但按观察性数据打折
<!-- 成本标签: 钱=0 时间=少 毅力=否 收益=小 口径=死亡率 -->
- 成本：不花钱，也不花时间。只要记住一点：这些数字说的是已婚的人里死亡率更低，是两件事同时出现，不是结婚让你活得久。
- 说人话：已婚的人同期死亡的概率比非婚的人低约 12%，从未结过婚的人比已婚的人高约 24%。但这只是两件事同时出现，不是结婚起的作用。本来健康、收入高、社交多的人，既更容易结婚，也更容易活得久。这些数字基本来自欧美，对国内只能当量级参考。
- 收益：一项针对老年人的荟萃分析，把多项研究汇总重算，共 53 组比较、25 万余人。已婚相对非婚的全因死亡 RR 0.88，95% CI 0.85–0.91（RR 是风险比，CI 是可信范围），同期死亡的概率低约 12%。同一项里丧偶 1.11、离异或分居 1.16、未婚 1.11，分别高约 11%、16%、11%。男女无差异。最保守的估计是 RR 0.94，只低约 6%。另一项荟萃分析比的是未婚（从未结婚）相对已婚，用了 95 篇文献、5 亿余人。结果 HR 1.24（1.19–1.30），同期死亡的概率高约 24%。而且年纪越大，差距越小。还有一项按性别拆的荟萃分析，21 项研究、789 万余人：不论男女，非婚都与总死亡、癌症死亡、心血管死亡同时出现。男性这边的心血管死亡和总死亡差距更大。未婚男性相对未婚女性，卒中死亡多 31%，全因死亡多 9%
- 证据等级：A（争议）
- 来源：Manzoli L, et al. (2007). Marital status and mortality in the elderly: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Soc Sci Med 64:77–94. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.socscimed.2006.08.031>；Roelfs DJ, et al. (2011). The rising relative risk of mortality for singles: meta-analysis and meta-regression. Am J Epidemiol 174(4):379–389. <https://doi.org/10.1093/aje/kwr111>；Wang Y, et al. (2020). Sex differences in the association between marital status and the risk of cardiovascular, cancer, and all-cause mortality: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 7,881,040 individuals. Glob Health Res Policy 5:4. <https://doi.org/10.1186/s41256-020-00133-8>
- 备注：争议在于结婚的人本来就是被挑过的：健康、收入高、社交多的人，既更容易结婚，也更容易活得久。三项荟萃用的都是现成人群的观察数据，只是跟踪记录，没有分组对照。作者自己也写了有发表偏倚或方法局限。Roelfs 还发现研究做得越严谨，算出的差距越小。这些数字以欧美人群为主，对国内只能当量级参考

### 8. Accounting for health benefits while adjusting for observational data
<!-- Cost Tag: Money=0 Time=Low Willpower=No Benefit=Low Metric=Mortality -->
- Cost: There is no cost in money or time. Just keep in mind that these figures reflect a lower mortality rate among married individuals — this simply means both conditions occur together, not that marriage itself extends life expectancy.
- In plain terms: Over a given period, married people have a roughly 12% lower chance of dying compared to unmarried individuals, while those who have never married face a roughly 24% higher risk. However, this merely shows a correlation between marital status and mortality; it does not prove that marriage directly causes longer life. People who are healthier, wealthier, and more socially active are both more likely to marry and more likely to live longer. These statistics are primarily drawn from European and North American populations, so they can only serve as rough benchmarks for China.
- Benefit: One meta-analysis of older adults pooled results from multiple studies, covering 53 comparisons and over 250,000 participants. It found that the relative risk of all-cause mortality for married versus unmarried individuals was RR 0.88, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.85–0.91. In other words, married people had a roughly 12% lower probability of dying during the study period. Among widowed individuals, this figure rose to 1.11; for divorced or separated persons, it was 1.16; and for those never married, it was 1.11 — indicating respective increases of about 11%, 16%, and 11% in mortality risk. No significant gender differences emerged. Under the most conservative estimates, the RR still came out at 0.94, reflecting a reduction of only around 6%. Another meta-analysis compared never-married individuals with married ones, drawing on 95 separate studies and over 500 million participants. It reported a hazard ratio of 1.24 (95% CI 1.19–1.30), meaning unmarried people faced roughly 24% higher mortality risk over the same timeframe; this gap narrowed with age. A further gender-specific meta-analysis examined 21 studies involving more than 7,890,000 individuals: across both sexes, unmarried status correlated with higher rates of overall mortality, cancer-related death, and cardiovascular death. Among men, the disparity was especially pronounced for cardiovascular and overall mortality; unmarried men also faced a 31% higher risk of stroke and a 9% higher risk of all-cause death compared to unmarried women.
- Evidence grade: A (controversial)
- Sources:Manzoli L, et al. (2007). Marital status and mortality in the elderly: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Soc Sci Med 64:77–94. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.socscimed.2006.08.031>; Roelfs DJ, et al. (2011). The rising relative risk of mortality for singles: meta-analysis and meta-regression. Am J Epidemiol 174(4):379–389. <https://doi.org/10.1093/aje/kwr111>; Wang Y, et al. (2020). Sex differences in the association between marital status and the risk of cardiovascular, cancer, and all-cause mortality: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 7,881,040 individuals. Glob Health Res Policy 5:4. <https://doi.org/10.1186/s41256-020-00133-8>
- Notes: The controversy stems from the fact that married individuals tend to be healthier, wealthier, and more socially engaged — factors that independently contribute to longer life. All three meta-analyses relied on observational data collected from existing populations; no controlled experiments or randomized groups were used. The authors themselves acknowledged potential publication bias and methodological limitations. Roelfs also noted that studies employing more rigorous methods tended to report smaller differences between marital groups. Since these figures are largely derived from Western populations, they can only be used as rough indicators for Chinese contexts.

title: 时间账按「无酬劳动」算，谈清分工再领证

originalText:
### 9. 时间账按「无酬劳动」算，谈清分工再领证
<!-- 成本标签: 钱=0 时间=中 毅力=些 收益=大 口径=时间 -->
- 成本：不花钱。婚前花一两个小时，把家务、照料老小、谁的工作让步这些没报酬的活谈成明确分工，之后按分工执行。难在把话摊开谈，别拖着不说。
- 说人话：全国时间利用调查里，家务和陪伴照料家人这类没报酬的活，男性每天平均 1 小时 52 分，女性 3 小时 29 分。调查没按结没结婚分组，所以「结了婚家务会多多少」没有官方数字，这个性别差距只能当上限参考。分工可以在领证前谈成另一个样子。
- 收益：2024 年全国时间利用调查。无酬劳动就是家务、陪伴照料家人这些没有报酬的活。当天做了这类活的人，每日平均花 2 小时 45 分，其中男性 1 小时 52 分、女性 3 小时 29 分。一天里做过这类活的人占多大比例，男性是 67.5%、女性是 83.9%。居民家务劳动每日平均 1 小时 17 分，只算做了的人是 1 小时 59 分，比 2018 年少 28 分。陪伴照料家人每日平均 30 分，只算做了的人是 1 小时 46 分。2018 年的数字是：家务劳动男性 45 分、女性 2 小时 6 分，陪伴照料孩子男性 17 分、女性 53 分
- 证据等级：A
- 来源：国家统计局 (2024). 第三次全国时间利用调查公报（第二号、第三号）. <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202410/t20241031_1957216.html>、<https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202410/t20241031_1957215.html>；国家统计局 (2019). 2018 年全国时间利用调查公报. <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202302/t20230203_1900224.html>
- 备注：两次调查都只按性别、城乡、年龄分组，没有按结没结婚分组。所以「结婚后家务会多多少」没有官方数字，只能用性别差距做上限参考。数字是全国平均，你们两个人的分工完全可以谈成另一个样子
englishText:
### 9. Discussing labor division before marriage helps clarify unpaid work responsibilities
<!-- Cost Tag: Money=0 Time=Med Willpower=Some Benefit=High Metric=Time -->

- Cost: There is no monetary cost. Spend one or two hours before marriage to reach a clear agreement on how household chores, childcare, and elder care — all unpaid tasks — will be divided between partners, then follow that plan. The real challenge lies in having the conversation, not in avoiding it.

- In plain terms: According to the 2024 National Time Use Survey, men spend an average of 1 hour and 52 minutes per day on unpaid activities such as housework and caring for family, while women spend 3 hours and 29 minutes. Since the survey does not break down data by marital status, there are no official figures on how much housework increases after marriage; the gender gap observed can only serve as an upper limit. In reality, couples can negotiate a different division of labor altogether before getting married.

- Benefit: The 2024 National Time Use Survey tracks unpaid labor, which includes housework and family care. On average, people who perform such tasks spend 2 hours and 45 minutes daily on them; men dedicate 1 hour and 52 minutes, women 3 hours and 29 minutes. The proportion of individuals engaging in unpaid labor each day is 67.5% among men and 83.9% among women. Nationwide, residents spend an average of 1 hour and 17 minutes daily on housework; among those who actually do it, the average rises to 1 hour and 59 minutes — a decrease of 28 minutes compared to 2018. Time spent caring for family averages 30 minutes per day; for those involved, it reaches 1 hour and 46 minutes. In 2018, men spent 45 minutes on housework and 17 minutes on childcare, while women spent 2 hours and 6 minutes on housework and 53 minutes on childcare.

- Evidence grade: A
- Sources:National Bureau of Statistics of China (2024). Bulletin of the Third National Time Use Survey (No. 2, No. 3). <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202410/t20241031_1957216.html>, <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202410/t20241031_1957215.html>; National Bureau of Statistics of China (2019). 2018 National Time Use Survey Bulletin. <https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202302/t20230203_1900224.html>

- Notes: Both surveys analyzed data only by gender, urban/rural residence, and age; marital status was not considered. Consequently, no official statistics exist on how much housework increases after marriage; the gender disparity can only be used as a rough upper bound. These figures represent national averages, but couples are free to negotiate a division of labor that suits them — and that is precisely the value of having this discussion.

### 10. 钱账先看法律默认规则，再决定要不要书面约定
<!-- 成本标签: 钱=0 时间=中 毅力=些 收益=大 口径=金钱 -->
- 成本：不花钱。读一遍民法典婚姻家庭编里讲财产的那几条。有需要就两个人签一份书面财产约定，法律只要求写成书面的，不必去公证。难在把钱的事提前说开。
- 说人话：不签书面约定的话，法律默认婚后挣的工资奖金、经营和投资收益、继承或受赠的财产都归两人共有。婚前财产、遗嘱或赠与合同写明只给一方的，才是个人的。两个人可以书面约定各归各，签了就有约束力。因带孩子、照料老人多付出的一方，离婚时可以要求补偿。
- 收益：不另作约定时的默认规则是：婚后所得的工资奖金劳务报酬、生产经营投资收益、知识产权收益、继承或受赠财产，归夫妻共同所有（第一千零六十二条）。婚前财产、人身损害赔偿、遗嘱或赠与合同明确只归一方的财产、一方专用生活用品，是个人财产（第一千零六十三条）。双方可以书面约定婚前和婚后财产归各自所有、共同所有，或者部分各自所有部分共同所有，这个约定对双方有法律约束力（第一千零六十五条）。因抚育子女、照料老人、协助另一方工作而负担较多义务的一方，离婚时有权请求补偿（第一千零八十八条）
- 证据等级：A
- 来源：全国人民代表大会 (2020). 中华人民共和国民法典（2021 年 1 月 1 日起施行，第一千零六十二、一千零六十三、一千零六十五、一千零八十八条）. 国家法律法规数据库 <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?title=%E4%B8%AD%E5%8D%8E%E4%BA%BA%E6%B0%91%E5%85%B1%E5%92%8C%E5%9B%BD%E6%B0%91%E6%B3%95%E5%85%B8&id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5c500bf>；条文全文见最高人民法院公报转载 <http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/7f184078694d811fb3314f6af9accf.html>
- 备注：彩礼、婚礼、婚房没有官方统计，本条不写数字。第一千零八十八条那笔补偿给多少，先由两人自己谈，谈不成由法院定，没有固定公式。书面财产约定对两边都管用：收入高的一方用得上，家务照料这类没报酬的活干得多的一方也用得上

### 10. First check the default legal rules regarding money and property, then decide whether to make a written agreement
<!-- Cost Tag: Money=0 Time=Med Willpower=Some Benefit=High Metric=Money -->

- Cost: There is no cost involved. Simply read the relevant articles in the Civil Code regarding marital property. If needed, the couple can sign a written property agreement; the law only requires it to be in writing, no notarization is necessary. The real challenge is discussing money matters openly beforehand.

- In plain terms: Without a written agreement, the law presumes that wages, bonuses, business profits, investment returns, inheritances, and gifts received after marriage belong to both spouses jointly. Only property owned before marriage, or items explicitly designated in a will or gift contract as belonging to one person, remain personal property. Couples may choose to agree in writing that certain assets stay separate; such an agreement becomes legally binding. A spouse who has devoted more time to raising children or caring for elderly relatives may request compensation during divorce proceedings.

- Benefit: By default, all earnings from employment, business activities, intellectual property, as well as inheritances and gifts received after marriage are considered joint marital property (Article 1062). Personal property includes assets owned prior to marriage, compensation for personal injury, items earmarked for one spouse in a will or gift contract, and everyday personal items (Article 1063). Couples may stipulate in writing whether their pre‑marital and post‑marital assets remain separate, become joint, or are divided partially; this arrangement is legally enforceable (Article 1065). The spouse who has shouldered greater responsibilities in child‑rearing, elder care, or supporting the other partner’s career may seek compensation upon divorce (Article 1088).

- Evidence grade: A
- Sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (effective from January 1, 2021, Articles 1062, 1063, 1065, 1088). National Laws and Regulations Database <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?title=%E4%B8%AD%E5%8D%8E%E4%BA%BA%E6%B0%91%E5%85%B1 %E5%92%8C%E5%9B%BD%E6%B0%91%E6%B3%95%E5%85%B8&id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5c500bf>; The full text of the article is reproduced in the Supreme People's Court of China communiqué <http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/7f184078694d811fb3314f6af9accf.html>

- Notes: No official statistics exist for dowries, wedding expenses, or marital homes, so no figures are provided here. The amount of compensation under Article 1088 is first negotiated between the couple; if they cannot reach an agreement, a court will decide it based on relevant circumstances. A written property agreement benefits both parties: it protects high‑earners and also safeguards those who perform unpaid domestic duties.

title: 父母出资买房，在转账的时候就把是借是送写清楚

originalText:
### 11. 父母出资买房，在转账的时候就把是借是送写清楚
<!-- 成本标签: 钱=0 时间=少 毅力=否 收益=大 口径=金钱 -->
- 成本：不花钱。出资当天写一页说明，写明这笔钱是赠与谁、还是借给谁，出资的父母和子女都签字。如果写的是借款，就让夫妻两个人都签，转账备注也写同一句话。

- 收益：婚前父母为双方购房出资的，认定为对自己子女个人的赠与。父母明确表示赠与双方的除外。婚后出资的，有约定按约定。没有约定或者约定不明确的，按夫妻共同财产的原则处理。2025 年 2 月 1 日起还有一条。婚内由一方父母全额出资、赠与合同又没写明只赠与自己子女的，离婚分割时，法院可以判房屋归出资人子女一方所有。判归之后再综合几项情况，确定要不要给另一方补偿、补多少。这几项是共同生活和生育共同子女的情况、离婚过错、对家庭的贡献大小、离婚时房屋市场价格。一方父母部分出资，或者双方父母都出资的，以出资来源和比例为基础判归其中一方，并合理补偿（全国）
- 证据等级：A
- 来源：最高人民法院 (2020). 关于适用《民法典》婚姻家庭编的解释（一）（法释〔2020〕22 号，第二十九条）. <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/282071.html>；最高人民法院 (2025). 关于适用《民法典》婚姻家庭编的解释（二）（法释〔2025〕1 号，第八条）. <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/452771.html>；全国人大 (2020). 民法典（第一千零六十二条第一款第四项）. <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>

### 11. When parents pay for a house, they should clearly state whether it’s a loan or a gift at the time of transfer
<!-- Cost Tag: Money=0 Time=Low Willpower=No Benefit=High Metric=Money -->

- Cost: There is no cost involved. On the day of payment, write a brief note specifying whether the money is a gift or a loan to the child. Both the parent(s) making the payment and the child must sign it. If it’s a loan, both spouses should also sign. Use the same wording in the transfer description.

- In plain terms: When parents pay for a house before marriage, the money is generally considered a gift solely to their own child. After marriage, without any written agreement, it’s treated as joint marital property. Starting February 2025, if one set of parents fully funds a house during marriage but the gift agreement doesn’t specify it’s only for their child, a court may award the house to that child upon divorce and decide whether to compensate the other spouse. To treat it as a loan, all terms must be clearly documented and signed on the same day.

- Benefit: Payments made by parents before marriage for a house are typically viewed as gifts to just one child, unless they explicitly state otherwise. After marriage, any agreement governs the arrangement; otherwise, it’s treated as joint property. Since February 2025, if one set of parents fully funds a house during marriage without specifying it’s only for their child, a court may award it to that child upon divorce and later determine if compensation is warranted. Factors considered include shared living arrangements, children born together, fault in the divorce, each party’s contributions, and current market value. Partial funding by one or both sets of parents results in a similar ruling, with compensation based on proportional contributions nationwide.

- Evidence grade: A
- Sources: Supreme People's Court of China (2020). Interpretation on the application of the marriage and family section of the Civil Code (1) (Fa Interpretation [2020] No. 22, Article 29). <https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/282071.html>; (Fa Interpretation [2025] No. 1, Article 8). <https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/452771.html>; National People’s Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 1062, Paragraph 1, Item 4). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>

- Notes: This rule applies to both parties involved. Parents no longer need to rely on a post-divorce loan agreement to protect their investment; post-February 2025, the source of funds itself determines ownership, independent of whose name appears on the title. Recipients of such funds also gain clarity early on. To treat it as a loan, all terms must be explicitly documented, signed, and reflected in the transfer description — otherwise, legal justification becomes necessary.

title: 配偶一方大额借的钱，你没签字也没追认，不自动变成你的债
englishTitle: Money borrowed by a spouse in a large amount — if you didn’t sign or later acknowledge it, it doesn’t automatically become your debt
originalText:
### 12. 配偶一方大额借的钱，你没签字也没追认，不自动变成你的债
<!-- 成本标签: 钱=0 时间=少 毅力=些 收益=大 口径=金钱 -->
- 成本：不花钱。别在配偶的借条、担保书上签「共同借款人」「担保人」。也别在聊天里写「这钱我们会还」这类话，它可能被当成你事后认下了这笔债。难在被催的时候忍住不接话。
- 说人话：配偶背着你借的钱，只要明显超出家里日常开销，你又没签字、没事后认账，就不自动变成你的债。要债的人得自己证明这钱用在了共同生活或共同经营上。但买房这种钱如果确实变成了你们一起住或共有的房子，对方往往证得到这一层。
- 收益：下面几种情形借的钱属于夫妻共同债务。一是夫妻双方共同签名的。二是一方事后追认，就是事后认下这笔债，两个人都认账。三是一方在婚内以个人名义为家庭日常生活需要借的。一方以个人名义借的、明显超出家庭日常开销的钱，不属于夫妻共同债务。例外是债权人（要债的一方）能证明这笔钱用于夫妻共同生活、共同生产经营，或者是两个人都认的账。买房的钱明显超出家庭日常生活需要，举证责任在主张债权的一方，要债的人得自己拿出证据。但这笔钱如果确实变成了夫妻共同居住或共有的房子，债权人往往能证到「用于夫妻共同生活」这一层。所以更管用的是第 11 条（父母出资时写清是借是送）那一步（全国，2021 年起）
- 证据等级：A
- 来源：全国人大 (2020). 民法典（第一千零六十四条）. <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>；最高人民法院 (2020 年第二次修正). 关于审理民间借贷案件适用法律若干问题的规定（第十五、十六条）. <http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/94b6623974526df7d2430a3c73f050.html>（最高人民法院公报）
- 备注：离婚分财产时，对方父母突然拿出一张只有配偶签字的借款协议，要分两步看。第一步看这笔借款到底有没有真发生。你说钱根本没交过，又能把理由说圆的，法院会结合几件事一起判断。先看借款金额、钱怎么交的、双方的经济能力，再看平时怎么交易、财产有没有相应变动、证人怎么说。对方只拿得出转账凭证的，仍要由他证明这笔借款成立。第二步，借款成立之后再看是不是共同债务。借条和担保书的一般规则见第 8 节第 18 条

### 12. Money borrowed by a spouse in a large amount — if you didn’t sign or later acknowledge it, it doesn’t automatically become your debt
<!-- Cost Tag: Money=0 Time=Low Willpower=Some Benefit=High Metric=Money -->

- Cost: No cost at all. Never sign “joint borrower” or “guarantor” on your spouse’s loan agreements or guarantee documents. Also avoid writing things like “We’ll pay back this money” in messages, as that could be taken as later acknowledgment of the debt. The hard part is staying silent when creditors start pressuring you.

- In plain terms: Money borrowed by a spouse behind your back generally won’t become your joint debt, provided it clearly exceeds normal household expenses and you neither signed any documents nor later acknowledged the debt. Creditors must prove the money was used for shared household needs or joint business activities. However, if the borrowed funds actually helped purchase a house that both of you now live in or own together, creditors can usually prove it served a shared purpose.

- Benefit: Debt is considered a joint marital obligation in several situations: first, when both spouses sign the loan agreement; second, when one spouse later acknowledges the debt, thereby accepting joint responsibility; third, when one spouse takes out a loan during marriage for ordinary household needs. Any loan taken out by one spouse that clearly exceeds everyday household expenses does not qualify as joint debt — unless the creditor can prove it was used for shared living or business purposes. Since buying a house typically exceeds normal household spending, the burden of proof falls on creditors to demonstrate such shared use. Yet if the house truly becomes a joint residence or property, creditors can more easily substantiate their claim. Thus, the key preventive measure is exactly what Section 11 describes: clearly stating whether parental contributions are loans or gifts (nationwide, effective since 2021).

- Evidence grade: A
- Sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 1064). <https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml>; Supreme People's Court of China (Second Amendment in 2020). Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases (Articles 15, 16). <http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/94b6623974526df7d2430a3c73f050.html> (Supreme People's Court of China Communique)

- Notes: During divorce proceedings, if one spouse’s parents suddenly produce a loan agreement bearing only their child’s signature, two distinct evaluations become necessary. First, courts must determine whether the loan actually occurred. If you can convincingly argue that no funds were transferred, judges will weigh multiple factors: loan amount, payment method, both parties’ financial standing, habitual transaction patterns, any corresponding property changes, and witness testimony. Mere possession of transfer records by creditors still obliges them to prove loan validity. Second, even if the loan is verified, its classification as joint debt must be re-examined. General rules governing loan agreements and guarantees are detailed in Section 8, Article 18.

originalText:
### 13. 领证只要身份证加一份签字声明，不用户口簿，不收钱，当场发证
<!-- 成本标签: 钱=0 时间=少 毅力=否 收益=小 口径=金钱 -->
- 成本：不花钱。两个人都要亲自到场。办完通常几十分钟。
- 说人话：2025 年 5 月起领证只要两样东西：本人身份证，加一份签字声明。声明里写明本人没有配偶，和对方没有直系血亲、三代以内旁系血亲关系。户口簿不用带，也不用回一方户口所在地办。登记一分钱不收，符合条件当场发证。
- 收益：2025 年 5 月 10 日起施行的新婚姻登记条例，改了内地居民结婚要交的材料。条文写的是只需出具两样东西：「（一）本人的居民身份证；（二）本人无配偶以及与对方当事人没有直系血亲和三代以内旁系血亲关系的签字声明」。户口簿不再是必需材料。登记机关是「县级人民政府民政部门或者省、自治区、直辖市人民政府按照便民原则确定的乡（镇）人民政府」。旧条例里「到一方当事人常住户口所在地」的限制已经取消。条例还写明「婚姻登记机关办理婚姻登记，不得收取费用」，以及「对当事人符合结婚条件的，应当当场予以登记，发给结婚证」
- 证据等级：A
- 来源：国务院 (2025). 婚姻登记条例（国令第 804 号，第二、六、八、十条）. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202504/content_7017752.htm>
- 备注：登记机关不给办的只有四种情况：没到法定结婚年龄，不是双方完全自愿，一方或双方已经有配偶，两人是直系血亲或三代以内旁系血亲。可能收费的只有照相、复印这类周边服务。登记本身一分钱不收，遇到「工本费」「加急费」直接拒绝并投诉。离婚登记的 30 天冷静期见本节退出成本那条

### 13. Obtaining a marriage certificate requires only an ID card and a signed declaration — no household register needed, no fees, and issuance is immediate.
<!-- Cost Tag: Money=0 Time=Low Willpower=No Benefit=Low Metric=Money -->

- Cost: There are no fees involved. Both parties must be present in person. The entire process typically takes just a few minutes.  
- In plain terms: Starting May 2025, getting a marriage certificate requires only two items: your ID card and a signed declaration stating that you have no spouse and share no direct or indirect blood relations within three generations with your partner. There’s no need to bring a household register, nor to go back to one’s place of hukou registration. The registration itself is completely free, and if all conditions are met, the certificate is issued on the spot.  
- Benefit: The revised Marriage Registration Regulations, effective May 10, 2025, streamlined documentation requirements for mainland residents. They specify that only two documents are mandatory: “(1) one’s own ID card; (2) a signed declaration confirming that one has no spouse and shares no direct or indirect blood relations within three generations with the other party.” The household register is no longer required. Registration is handled by “county-level civil affairs bureaus or township governments designated by provincial or municipal authorities to ensure accessibility.” The previous requirement to register at the hukou location of one partner has been removed. The regulations also explicitly state that “marriage registration authorities must not charge any fees” and “must issue certificates on the spot to applicants who meet all eligibility criteria.”  
- Evidence grade: A  
- Sources:State Council of China (2025). Marriage Registration Regulations (National Order No. 804, Articles 2, 6, 8, and 10). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202504/content_7017752.htm>
- Notes: Registration will be denied only in four cases: if either party is under legal marriage age, if consent is not mutual, if either party already has a spouse, or if the couple shares direct or indirect blood relations within three generations. Any additional charges usually apply only to optional services such as photography or photocopying — the registration process itself remains free. If anyone demands a “processing fee” or “express service charge,” such demands should be refused and reported. The 30-day cooling-off period for divorce registration is discussed under the “Cost” section.

The registration itself is completely free, and if all conditions are met, the certificate is issued on the spot.

### 14. Undergoing a premarital medical exam: if a serious illness is present, it must be disclosed before marriage registration
<!-- Cost Tag: Money=Low Time=Low Willpower=No Benefit=Med Metric=Mortality -->
- Cost: In most regions, the exam is provided free of charge or at a reduced cost for eligible individuals; otherwise it costs only a few hundred yuan. The procedure itself takes about half a day.
- In plain terms: If a person has a serious illness and fails to disclose it truthfully before marriage registration, the other spouse may petition a court to annul the marriage. Additional policies encourage locating exam facilities near marriage registration offices and offering integrated services that combine registration, medical screening, and fertility counseling. The Civil Code likewise mandates disclosure of serious illnesses prior to marriage; non‑compliance grants the other spouse the right to seek annulment within one year of becoming aware of the condition.

originalText:
### 15. 算退出成本：协议离婚有 30 天冷静期，诉讼离婚有法定条件
<!-- 成本标签: 钱=0 时间=中 毅力=些 收益=大 口径=金钱 -->
- 成本：不花钱。婚前花点时间读一遍：万一要退出，要花多久，走什么程序。难在结婚前就去想散伙的事。
- 说人话：协议离婚不是签完就完。交了申请后 30 天内，任何一方都能撤回。期满还要在 30 天内两人亲自去领离婚证，不去就当撤回。对方不同意，只能起诉。法院先调解，要有家暴、重婚、分居满两年这些情形，调解不成才判离。
- 收益：协议离婚要签书面离婚协议，并亲自到婚姻登记机关申请（第一千零七十六条）。自登记机关收到申请之日起 30 日内，任何一方可以撤回。期满后 30 日内，双方须亲自申领离婚证，不申领视为撤回（第一千零七十七条）。一方不同意时走诉讼，法院应先调解。有重婚或与他人同居、家庭暴力或虐待遗弃、赌博吸毒屡教不改、因感情不和分居满二年等情形的，调解无效应准予离婚。判不离后又分居满一年，再起诉应准予（第一千零七十九条）。2024 年全国离婚 351.3 万对，其中 89.1 万对走的是法院判决、调解
- 证据等级：A
- 来源：全国人民代表大会 (2020). 中华人民共和国民法典（第一千零七十六、一千零七十七、一千零七十九条）. <http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/7f184078694d811fb3314f6af9accf.html>；民政部 (2020). 关于贯彻落实《中华人民共和国民法典》中有关婚姻登记规定的通知（民发〔2020〕116 号）. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-12/04/content_5567010.htm>；民政部 (2025). 2024 年民政事业发展统计公报. 题录同第 7 条（结婚率、离婚率各是什么口径）

### 15. Calculating the cost of walking away: Divorce by mutual agreement requires a 30-day cooling-off period, while divorce via litigation has strict legal prerequisites.
<!-- Cost Tag: Money=0 Time=Med Willpower=Some Benefit=High Metric=Money -->

- Cost: There is no monetary cost. However, it’s worth spending some time before marriage to consider how long it might take and what steps would be required to end the marriage, should that ever become necessary. The real challenge lies in contemplating a potential separation before tying the knot.

- In plain terms: Divorce by mutual consent isn’t finalized the moment the paperwork is signed. Within 30 days of filing the application, either spouse may withdraw it. After that window closes, both parties must appear in person within another 30 days to obtain the divorce certificate; failure to do so also counts as a withdrawal. If one spouse refuses to cooperate, the other must pursue litigation. Courts first attempt mediation; only when circumstances such as domestic violence, bigamy, or two years of separation persist without resolution will a divorce be granted.

- Benefit: Under Article 1076 of the law, divorce by mutual agreement necessitates a written agreement and joint application to the marriage registry. Within 30 days of submission, either party may withdraw the request. Following this period, both spouses must apply for the certificate within a further 30 days; otherwise, the application is deemed withdrawn (Article 1077). In contested cases, courts must first mediate. Divorce is permitted when evidence of bigamy, cohabitation with another, domestic abuse, substance abuse, or two years of separation exists, even if mediation fails (Article 1079). Subsequent to a denial, another year of separation followed by renewed litigation also qualifies for approval. In 2024, 3.513 million couples divorced nationwide, of which 891,000 relied on court rulings or mediation.

- Evidence grade: A
- Sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (Articles 1076, 1077, 1079). <http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/7f184078694d811fb3314f6af9accf.html>; Ministry of Civil Affairs of China (2020). Notice on the implementation of the provisions on marriage registration in the "Civil Code of the People's Republic of China" (Minfa [2020] No. 116). <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-12/04/content_5567010.htm>; Ministry of Civil Affairs of China (2025). 2024 Statistical Bulletin on the Development of Civil Affairs. The title is the same as Article 7 (what are the marriage rates and divorce rates?)

- Notes: The cooling-off period applies exclusively to divorce by mutual agreement; litigation entails no such pause but involves lengthier proceedings. Fees for court filings and legal representation vary regionally, hence exact figures are omitted here. While the procedural hurdles may seem considerable, they shouldn’t deter marriage; rather, they underscore the importance of awareness prior to committing.

### 16. 给「为长辈结婚」单独记一笔账，别和自己的账混在一起
<!-- 成本标签: 钱=0 时间=少 毅力=些 收益=中 口径=时间 -->
- 成本：不花钱。在纸上分两栏写。一栏是这段婚姻里哪些收益是你自己的，本节前面几条能算出来。另一栏是哪些收益是长辈的：安心、面子、催婚停止。难在把长辈那一栏单独放着，不往自己这栏里并。
- 说人话：长辈那份收益，也就是安心、面子、不再催，是真的。但它不会自动变成你的健康收益或关系质量。而时间账、钱账和退出成本这三笔，全部由你自己承担。在纸上分两栏，把哪些收益归自己、哪些归长辈写开，这笔账划不划算自己一眼就能看出来。
- 收益：长辈的收益是真实的。但它不会自动转成你的健康收益（第 8 条）或关系质量（第 4 条，关系好不好看自己的感受）。而时间账（第 9 条）、钱账（第 10 到 12 条）和退出成本（第 15 条），全部由当事人承担。分开记账以后，「做任务式结婚」的性价比是高是低，自己就能看出来

### 16. Make a separate tally for the benefits to your elders when they get married — don’t mix it with your own records.
<!-- Cost Tag: Money=0 Time=Low Willpower=Some Benefit=Med Metric=Time -->
- Cost: No cost at all. Just draw two columns on paper. One column lists the benefits that go to you from this marriage — you can calculate those using the earlier sections. The other column lists the benefits that go to your elders: peace of mind, social prestige, and an end to pressure to marry. The hard part is keeping the elders’ column separate and not merging it with yours.
- In plain terms: The benefits your elders gain — peace of mind, social standing, and relief from marriage pressure — are very real. But they won’t automatically translate into better health outcomes or improved relationship quality for you. Meanwhile, the time costs, financial outlays, and exit costs all fall squarely on your shoulders. By drawing two columns on paper and assigning each benefit to the right party, you can instantly see whether this arrangement is worth it for you.
- Benefit: The benefits your elders receive are genuine. All time costs (Section 9), financial expenses (Sections 10–12), and exit costs (Section 15) must be borne by you. - Evidence grade: C

title: 把关系好坏当成一笔健康账：吵架对事不对人，别骂人、别挖苦
englishTitle: Treating relationship quality as a health factor: focus on the issue, not the person — avoid insults and sarcasm
originalText:
### 17. 把关系好坏当成一笔健康账：吵架对事不对人，别骂人、别挖苦
<!-- 成本标签: 钱=0 时间=少 毅力=些 收益=小 口径=死亡率 -->
- 成本：不花钱。吵架时只说眼前这件事，不骂人，不挖苦，不翻旧账。难在气头上管住嘴。
- 说人话：夫妻关系好的，身体好一些，死亡风险也低一些。这个关联不大，和饮食对健康的关联差不多大。一项实验里，吵架时一直带着敌意的夫妻，实验做出的小伤口愈合速度只有平和夫妻的六成。
- 收益：把 126 篇研究、7.2 万多人合起来算（荟萃分析）。婚姻质量越高，身体越好，相关系数 r 在 .07 到 .21 之间。相关系数 0 是毫无关系，1 是完全同步。其中和死亡风险更低的相关是 r = .11。吵架时心血管反应更小，r = -.13。作者说，这些效应都小，和饮食这类健康习惯与健康的关联差不多大。另一项交叉实验里，42 对健康夫妻各住院两次，每次 24 小时。一次做互相支持的谈话，一次讨论一件有分歧的事。吵完之后，实验做出的水泡伤口愈合更慢。两次都表现出更多敌意的夫妻，伤口愈合速度只有低敌意夫妻的 60%。吵架第二天早上，他们血里的炎症指标（IL-6、肿瘤坏死因子）也升得更多。
- 证据等级：B
- 来源：Robles TF, Slatcher RB, Trombello JM, McGinn MM (2014). Marital quality and health: a meta-analytic review. Psychological Bulletin. <https://doi.org/10.1037/a0031859>；Kiecolt-Glaser JK 等 (2005). Hostile marital interactions, proinflammatory cytokine production, and wound healing. Archives of General Psychiatry. <https://doi.org/10.1001/archpsyc.62.12.1377>
- 备注：定 B 的理由：汇总的研究大多只是跟踪记录，没有分组对照。所以分不清是关系差让人生病，还是身体差让关系变差。有的研究扣掉年龄和收入之后，关联仍然在。Robles 原文还写明，一部分结果有发表偏倚。明确比较过男女的研究，基本没发现男女不同。本节没有找到直接比较「关系差的婚姻」和「不结婚」死亡率的汇总分析，所以「坏婚姻比不结婚更伤身」只能算推论。伤口实验只有 42 对夫妻。「对事不对人，不骂人不挖苦」是作者从实验里的「敌意行为」推出来的做法，没有研究直接比较过。吵得凶又改不了，两个人一起去做伴侣治疗，见本节第 20 条（伴侣治疗）。吵到动手，或者长期辱骂、威胁，就不是沟通问题了，是家暴，见第 8 节第 43 条（被家暴了）。想清楚要不要走，退出成本见本节第 15 条（退出成本）。

### 17. Treating relationship quality as a health factor: focus on the issue, not the person — avoid insults and sarcasm
<!-- Cost Tag: Money=0 Time=Low Willpower=Some Benefit=Low Metric=Mortality -->

- Cost: No cost at all. When arguing, stick to the current issue only; do not insult, mock, or bring up past grievances. The real challenge is keeping your mouth in check when angry.

- In plain terms: Couples with a good relationship tend to be healthier and have a lower risk of mortality. This link is relatively weak — comparable to how diet affects health. In one experiment, wounds on partners who remained hostile during arguments healed at only 60% of the rate seen in couples who stayed calm.

- Benefit: This conclusion comes from a meta-analysis of 126 studies involving over 72,000 participants. Higher marital quality correlates with better health, with correlation coefficients ranging from 0.07 to 0.21 (where 0 means no link and 1 means perfect alignment). The strongest association is with reduced mortality, at r = 0.11. Additionally, hostile arguments lead to a weaker cardiovascular response, with r = -0.13. These effects are modest, similar in magnitude to those linked to dietary habits. In another controlled experiment, 42 healthy couples were hospitalized twice for 24 hours each: once for supportive conversation and once to discuss a contentious issue. After the argument, wounds healed more slowly; couples displaying greater hostility saw healing at just 60% of the rate seen in low‑hostility pairs. The next morning, their blood showed higher levels of inflammatory markers such as IL‑6 and tumor necrosis factor.

- Evidence grade: B
- Sources:Robles TF, Slatcher RB, Trombello JM, McGinn MM (2014). Marital quality and health: a meta-analytic review. Psychological Bulletin. <https://doi.org/10.1037/a0031859>; Kiecolt-Glaser JK et al. (2005). Hostile marital interactions, proinflammatory cytokine production, and wound healing. Archives of General Psychiatry. <https://doi.org/10.1001/archpsyc.62.12.1377>

- Notes: The B rating reflects that most included studies were observational and lacked controlled groups, making it hard to determine whether poor relationships cause health problems or vice versa. Even after adjusting for age and income, some associations persisted. The original study also notes potential publication bias. Gender differences were not evident in studies that compared men and women. No meta‑analysis directly compares mortality rates between couples in bad marriages and those who remain unmarried; thus the claim that “bad marriages are worse for health than staying single” remains a hypothesis. The wound‑healing experiments involved only 42 couples. The advice “focus on the issue, not the person — avoid insults and sarcasm” is derived from observed hostile behaviors in those studies; no research has directly tested this approach. If arguments persist despite these efforts, couples may consider couple therapy (see Section 20). Physical violence, chronic insults, or threats go beyond communication issues and constitute domestic abuse (see Section 8, Item 43). For guidance on whether to leave a relationship and the associated costs, see Section 15 on exit costs.

originalText:
### 18. 同性伴侣趁两个人都清醒，办好授权委托、意定监护和遗嘱：法律上你们不是近亲属，不办就没有签字权和继承权
<!-- 成本标签: 钱=少 时间=中 毅力=些 收益=大 口径=自由 -->
- 成本：意定监护和遗嘱去公证处办，公证费各地不同，几百元起。自己手写遗嘱不花钱。前后要花一两个半天。难在两个人要坐下来谈生病和死。
- 说人话：法律上的近亲属是配偶、父母、子女、兄弟姐妹这些人，伴侣不算。不提前办文件，一方病重时，另一方替他做不了主。一方去世时，另一方一分遗产也继承不到。三份文件各管一段：活着时靠授权委托，失去判断能力后靠意定监护，身后靠遗嘱。
- 收益：民法典第一千零四十五条列的近亲属是配偶、父母、子女、兄弟姐妹、祖父母、外祖父母、孙子女、外孙子女。第一千一百二十七条的法定继承人先是配偶、子女、父母，其次是兄弟姐妹、祖父母、外祖父母。伴侣两处都不在。第一千二百一十九条管的是手术、特殊检查、特殊治疗。不能或者不宜向患者说明的，医务人员要向患者的「近亲属」说明，并取得同意。有三条路可以补上。第一，第三十三条允许成年人和「其他愿意担任监护人的个人」事先书面约定监护人。本人丧失或者部分丧失民事行为能力后，这个人来当监护人，监护人就是法定代理人。第二，第一百六十五条规定，书面授权委托书要写明代理人的姓名、代理事项、权限和期限，由本人签名或者盖章。本人一去世，委托就终止。第三，第一千一百三十三条允许立遗嘱，把个人财产赠给法定继承人以外的个人。湖北省司法厅网站刊登的宜昌市司法局文章写明，同性伴侣可以办意定监护协议公证，指定对方当自己将来的监护人（全国）
- 证据等级：A
- 来源：全国人大 (2020). 民法典（第二十三、三十三、一百六十五、一百七十三、一千零四十五、一千一百二十四、一千一百二十七、一千一百三十三至一千一百四十、一千一百四十二、一千二百一十九条）. <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5c500bf>（国家法律法规数据库）；宜昌市司法局 (2021). 意定监护公证：通向彩虹的公证之路. 湖北省司法厅网站「实践荟萃」栏目. <https://sft.hubei.gov.cn/fbjd/sjhc/202101/t20210108_3208602.shtml>
- 备注：伴侣拿遗产的身份是「受遗赠人」，不是继承人。知道有这份遗赠后，60 天内要明确表示接受，不表示就算放弃。伴侣本人和跟他有利害关系的人，不能当遗嘱见证人。立了几份遗嘱，以最后一份为准，见第 17 节第 2 条（遗嘱后立的推翻先立的）。意定监护人能不能直接签手术同意书，各医院做法不一，提前问一下常去的医院。家属不认这些文件，就要打官司：一审普通程序 6 个月起，律师费自己出。所以文件尽量去公证处办。一起买的房子、一起存的钱，按真实出资另外写书面约定。意定监护怎么办，见第 17 节第 1 条（书面指定将来的监护人）。受益人是你自己和伴侣。

### 18. Same-sex partners should prepare a power of attorney, a voluntary guardianship agreement, and a will while both are still lucid: legally, you are not considered close relatives, so without these documents you’ll have no right to sign on behalf of each other or to inherit anything.
<!-- Cost Tag: Money=Low Time=Med Willpower=Some Benefit=High Metric=Freedom -->

- Cost: Notarizing a voluntary guardianship agreement and a will incurs fees that vary by region, typically starting at a few hundred yuan. Drafting a handwritten will costs nothing. The whole process usually takes one or two half‑days; the real challenge is getting both partners to discuss illness and death openly.

- In plain terms: Under the law, close relatives include spouses, parents, children, and siblings — partners do not qualify. If no paperwork is done beforehand, when one partner becomes seriously ill the other cannot make medical decisions for them, and upon death the surviving partner receives no inheritance. These three documents each serve a distinct purpose: the power of attorney covers everyday decisions while both are capable; the voluntary guardianship kicks in if one loses decision‑making ability; the will governs what happens after death.

- Benefit: Article 1045 of the Civil Code lists close relatives as spouses, parents, children, siblings, grandparents, and grandchildren. Article 1127 defines legal heirs as spouses, children, parents, then siblings and grandparents. Partners appear in neither category. Article 1219 addresses surgeries, special tests, and treatments: if full disclosure to the patient isn’t possible, doctors must inform and obtain consent from “close relatives.” Three legal pathways can fill this gap. First, Article 33 permits adults to enter a written agreement designating another adult as their guardian; that person then acts as a legal representative. Second, Article 165 requires a power of attorney that names the agent, outlines duties, and is signed by the principal; this arrangement ends upon the principal’s death. Third, Article 1133 allows a will to leave property to anyone outside the statutory heir list. According to a published article by the Yichang Judicial Bureau, same‑sex couples may notarize a voluntary guardianship agreement naming their partner as future guardian — a practice now recognized nationwide.

- Evidence grade: A
- Sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 23, 33, 165, 173, 1045, 1124, 1127, 1133 to 1140, 1142, 1219). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5c500bf> (National Laws and Regulations Database); Yichang Municipal Justice Bureau (2021). Notarization of Intentional Guardianship: The Notarization Road to the Rainbow. "Practice Collection" column of the Hubei Provincial Department of Justice website. <https://sft.hubei.gov.cn/fbjd/sjhc/202101/t20210108_3208602.shtml>

- Notes: In a will, a partner is classified as a “legatee” rather than an heir. Once aware of the bequest, the partner must explicitly accept it within 60 days; otherwise the gift is forfeited. Neither the partner nor anyone with a conflict of interest may serve as a witness. If multiple wills exist, the most recent one supersedes earlier versions, as noted in Section 17.2. Hospitals differ on whether a voluntary guardian can sign consent forms; it’s wise to verify this with your regular medical facility. Should family members dispute these documents, litigation may ensue — first‑instance trials typically last at least six months, with legal fees borne by the parties. For that reason, having the documents notarized is advisable. Any jointly purchased property or shared savings should be documented separately with clear statements of each party’s contribution. Guidance on establishing voluntary guardianship can be found in Section 17.1. The ultimate beneficiaries of all these arrangements are you and your partner.

originalText:
### 19. 别靠隐瞒性取向结婚，也别把形婚当成省事的办法：法律上它就是一段真婚姻，想退出只能走离婚
<!-- 成本标签: 钱=0 时间=少 毅力=是 收益=中 口径=金钱 -->

### 19. Don’t marry while hiding your sexual orientation, and don’t treat “marriage of convenience” as an easy shortcut: legally, it is a real marriage, and the only way out is divorce.
<!-- Cost Tag: Money=0 Time=Low Willpower=Yes Benefit=Med Metric=Money -->

- Cost: There is no financial cost. The hard part is resisting family pressure to stay married — this may go on for many years.

- In plain terms: Marrying while concealing one’s sexual orientation is not legally invalid, nor can it be annulled; the only way to end it is through divorce. A “marriage of convenience” is also a real marriage, so any income earned or debts incurred afterward are treated as joint marital property. When the deceived spouse files for divorce, they may request a larger share of assets and compensation for emotional distress, though whether the court will grant this remains uncertain.

- Benefit: Article 1051 of the Civil Code lists only three grounds on which a marriage can be declared invalid: bigamy, prohibited familial relationships, and underage marriage. Articles 1052 and 1053 allow annulment only in cases of coercion or concealed serious illnesses prior to marriage. Interpretation (I) of the Marriage and Family Section, Article 17, states that any other grounds for invalidation will be rejected by courts. Hence, divorce is the sole legal exit route. A registered “marriage of convenience” is likewise lawful. Article 1062 designates post‑marriage wages, bonuses, and other earnings as joint property, while Article 1064 treats debts jointly signed or incurred for household needs as joint obligations. Divorce damages are covered in Article 1091, limited to bigamy, cohabitation with a third party, domestic violence, abuse, abandonment, or “other major faults”; Interpretation (I), Article 2 restricts “cohabitation with a third party” to opposite‑sex relationships. Thus, same‑sex relationships must rely on the “other major faults” clause for compensation claims, which may include emotional distress awards — these must be requested at the time of filing for divorce, otherwise they won’t be granted. No court rulings on such cases have been published since the Civil Code took effect; however, a 2013 article on the Jiangsu Provincial Higher People’s Court website discussed a wife suing for divorce after discovering her husband’s homosexuality, presenting two viewpoints: one argued that homosexuality did not qualify as a statutory fault, so no extra assets or compensation should be awarded; the author supported the opposite stance, advocating that the deceived spouse be treated as “innocent” and thus entitled to asset protection and emotional damages nationwide.

- Evidence grade: A
- Sources: National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 1051 to 1054, 1062, 1064, 1079, 1087, 1091). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5c500bf> (National Laws and Regulations Database); Supreme People's Court of China (2020). Interpretation on the application of the marriage and family section of the "Civil Code of the People's Republic of China" (1) (Fa Interpretation [2020] No. 22, Articles 2, 17, 86 to 90). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff80808177e75f880178006736f21aaf>; Zhu Laikuan, Wang Hongjuan (2013). Can damages be claimed for divorce due to homosexuality? Jiangsu Court Network. <http://www.jsfy.gov.cn/article/26621.html>

- Notes: Only one analytical article mentions the possibility of extra assets and emotional compensation; it does not describe any actual verdict, so success depends on the specific court. The Civil Code introduced “other major faults” as a new legal basis, giving the deceived spouse a stronger argument. The statutory provisions themselves merit an A rating. If both parties in a “marriage of convenience” each have same‑sex partners, those partners receive no marital protections, and any related property arrangements must be specified separately — see Section 18 on same‑sex guardianship and wills. Divorce procedures, including the 30‑day cooling‑off period or litigation, follow the same rules as any other divorce; see Section 15. Waiving compensation claims in a divorce agreement bars any later legal pursuit. The primary beneficiaries are the deceived spouse; the other party also faces consequences such as divorce, asset division, and child‑custody disputes once the deception is uncovered.

### 20. 关系卡在反复吵架和冷战里，两个人一起去做伴侣治疗：干等着基本不会自己好
<!-- 成本标签: 钱=多 时间=中 毅力=是 收益=中 口径=时间 -->
- 成本：要花钱。按次收费，各地各医院不一样，本条不写数字。研究里一般每周去一次，一项试验前后做了约 8 个月。难在两个人都得去，还得坚持做完。
- 说人话：关系卡住的伴侣一起做完伴侣治疗，对这段关系明显满意多了，大约七成有好转。光排队干等的伴侣，基本没变化。但效果会变淡：跟到第 5 年，约一半还明显好着，约四分之一已经分居或离婚。
- 收益：2020 年一项荟萃分析汇总了 58 项研究、2092 对伴侣。做完伴侣治疗，关系满意度的前后变化 g = 1.12（可信范围 0.92–1.31），作者说是大效应。g 是效应量，见 README 术语表。分到排队等候的伴侣，同一段时间 g = 0.12（−0.04 到 0.29），没有明显改善。开始时关系越差的，改善反而越多。2012 年一篇综述写的是，伴侣治疗让 70% 接受治疗的伴侣有好转。另一项随机试验找了 134 对长期、严重不和的夫妻，做了约 8 个月的两种行为伴侣治疗。做完时满意度变化 d = 0.90 和 0.71。到第 5 年，两种做法分别有 50.0% 和 45.9% 的夫妻仍有明显好转。这里的明显好转，作者叫「有临床意义的改善」。同时有 25.7% 和 27.9% 已经分居或离婚
- 证据等级：A（争议）
- 来源：Roddy MK, Walsh LM, Rothman K, Hatch SG, Doss BD (2020). Meta-analysis of couple therapy: effects across outcomes, designs, timeframes, and other moderators. Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology, 88(7), 583-596. <https://doi.org/10.1037/ccp0000514>；Lebow JL, Chambers AL, Christensen A, Johnson SM (2012). Research on the treatment of couple distress. Journal of Marital and Family Therapy, 38(1), 145-168. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1752-0606.2011.00249.x>；Christensen A, Atkins DC, Baucom B, Yi J (2010). Marital status and satisfaction five years following a randomized clinical trial comparing traditional versus integrative behavioral couple therapy. Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology, 78(2), 225-235. <https://doi.org/10.1037/a0018132>；Rathgeber M, Bürkner PC, Schiller EM, Holling H (2019). The efficacy of emotionally focused couples therapy and behavioral couples therapy: a meta-analysis. Journal of Marital and Family Therapy, 45(3), 447-463. <https://doi.org/10.1111/jmft.12336>（争议方）；Shadish WR, Baldwin SA (2003). Meta-analysis of MFT interventions. Journal of Marital and Family Therapy, 29(4), 547-570. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1752-0606.2003.tb01694.x>（争议方）；Karakurt G, Whiting K, van Esch C, Bolen SD, Calabrese JR (2016). Couples therapy for intimate partner violence: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Journal of Marital and Family Therapy, 42(4), 567-583. <https://doi.org/10.1111/jmft.12178>；全国人大常委会 (2018 修正). 精神卫生法（第二十三、五十一条）. <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf7448a066d>（国家法律法规数据库）
- 备注：争议在效果能保持多久。只收随机试验的另一项荟萃分析里，做完时 g = 0.60，半年后 0.44。到 12 个月只剩行为伴侣治疗有数据，g = 0.06，几乎没保住。另一篇汇总 20 项荟萃分析的综述说，有临床意义的效果出现在 40% 到 50% 的人身上。「七成好转」和「四到五成明显好转」用的标准不一样，别混着比。5 年那项试验没有不做治疗的对照，所以说不清离婚是变多还是变少了。2020 年那项汇总的全是异性伴侣，本条也没有找到国内的随机试验，套到自己身上要打折。国内去哪做：精神卫生法规定心理治疗要在医疗机构里做，心理咨询人员不得做心理治疗。可以去医院的精神科、心理科问有没有夫妻治疗。在医院外找机构，先问清对方的资质和受过什么训练。有家暴的先别一起做。2016 年那项荟萃分析写明，结论只适用于轻到中度、双方因冲突动手的情况。以控制对方、严重伤害为特征的暴力不在其内。业内也担心谈完回家遭报复。被打了先看第 8 节第 43 条（被家暴了）。吵架时怎么说话见本节第 17 条（吵架对事不对人），想清楚要不要走见本节第 15 条（退出成本）。受益人是你自己和配偶。

### 20. When a relationship is stuck in endless arguments and silent treatment, couples therapy can help — waiting alone rarely does
<!-- Cost Tag: Money=High Time=Med Willpower=Yes Benefit=Med Metric=Time -->

- Cost: Couples therapy comes at a cost. Fees are charged per session and vary by location and clinic; no exact figures are provided here. Typically, participants attend weekly sessions over a period of about eight months. The main challenge is that both partners must attend regularly and see it through to the end.

- In plain terms: Couples who attend therapy together tend to report significantly higher relationship satisfaction — roughly 70% experience noticeable improvement. In contrast, couples who simply wait without any intervention show little to no change. However, these benefits tend to fade over time: after five years, about half of those who sought therapy still report clear gains, while roughly a quarter end up separated or divorced.

- Benefit: A 2020 meta-analysis examined 58 studies involving 2,092 couples. After completing therapy, the average change in relationship satisfaction was g = 1.12 (95% CI: 0.92–1.31), which researchers consider a large effect size. g is an effect size measure; see the glossary for details. For couples who only waited without therapy, the same period yielded g = 0.12 (−0.04 to 0.29), indicating virtually no improvement. The greater the initial dissatisfaction, the larger the subsequent gain. Another review from 2012 reported that 70% of couples receiving therapy showed positive outcomes. One randomized trial followed 134 long‑married couples with serious conflicts; after eight months of two different behavioral therapy programs, satisfaction improved by d = 0.90 and d = 0.71 respectively. Five years later, 50.0% and 45.9% of those couples still showed clinically meaningful improvement. At the same time, 25.7% and 27.9% had separated or divorced.

- Evidence grade: A (controversial)
- Sources: Roddy MK, Walsh LM, Rothman K, Hatch SG, Doss BD (2020). Meta-analysis of couple therapy: effects across outcomes, designs, timeframes, and other moderators. Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology, 88(7), 583-596. <https://doi.org/10.1037/ccp0000514>; Lebow JL, Chambers AL, Christensen A, Johnson SM (2012). Research on the treatment of couple distress. Journal of Marital and Family Therapy, 38(1), 145-168. Christensen A, Atkins DC, Baucom B, Yi J (2010). Marital status and satisfaction five years following a Randomized clinical trial comparing traditional versus integrative behavioral couple therapy. Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology, 78(2), 225-235. <https://doi.org/10.1037/a0018132>; Rathgeber M, Bürkner PC, Schiller EM, Holling H (2019). The efficacy of emotionally focused couples therapy and behavioral couples therapy: a meta-analysis. Journal of Marital and Family Therapy, 45(3), 447-463. <https://doi.org/10.1111/jmft.12336> (Disputant); Shadish WR, Baldwin SA (2003). Meta-analysis of MFT interventions. Journal of Marital and Family Therapy, 29(4), 547-570. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1752-0606.2003.tb01694.x> (disputing party); Karakurt G, Whiting K, van Esch C, Bolen SD, Calabrese JR (2016). Couples therapy for intimate partner violence: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Journal of Marital and Family Therapy, 42(4), 567-583. <https://doi.org/10.1111/jmft.12178>; National People's Congress Standing Committee (2018 revision). Mental Health Law (Article 23, 51). <https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf7448a066d> (National Laws and Regulations Database)

- Notes: The main controversy concerns how long these benefits actually last. Another meta-analysis limited to randomized trials found g = 0.60 right after therapy and g = 0.44 after six months; by twelve months only one behavioral therapy approach retained any measurable effect, with g = 0.06 — essentially negligible. A broader review of 20 meta-analyses concluded that clinically meaningful improvement occurs in 40% to 50% of participants. The figures “70% improvement” and “40–50% clinically meaningful improvement” refer to different criteria and should not be directly compared. The five‑year trial lacked a control group of couples receiving no treatment, so it is unclear whether divorce rates rose or fell. The 2020 meta‑analysis included only heterosexual couples; no comparable randomized trials have been identified in China, so results should be interpreted with caution. In China, mental health regulations require that psychotherapy be delivered within medical institutions; counselors without medical qualifications may not provide psychotherapy. You can inquire at psychiatric or psychology departments of hospitals about available couples therapy programs. If seeking outside a hospital, verify the practitioner’s credentials and training. Couples experiencing domestic violence should not begin therapy together. A 2016 meta‑analysis noted that its conclusions apply only to mild‑to‑moderate conflicts where both partners occasionally engage in physical altercations; it does not cover situations dominated by controlling or severely harmful behavior. There is also concern that returning home after therapy might increase the risk of retaliation. If you have been physically abused, see Section 8, Item 43. For advice on how to talk during arguments, see Section 17; for guidance on whether to end the relationship, see Section 15. The primary beneficiaries of therapy are both you and your spouse.
